posts.author: Rvanbergen
posts.body:
I want to make a Pokémon Parody, and I need a battle system that somewhat resembles the Pokémon one. Because RPG Maker has problems with the "switch out" mechanic, I came up with my own compromise. But after thinking about it for so long, my brain is tired, and so I decided to crowdsource it.
Here's how my hypothetical system works: (The red parts are my questions)
The party consists of two members: The Trainer and one of the Pokémon. There will also be three Pokémon in the reserve party eventually, though not at the start.
The Trainer always selects first.
How do I do this? Do I just set their Speed is as high as can go?
How do I make it so the opponent never targets them?
During their turn the Trainer has 4 choices:
"Pokémon", where they can switch out the active Pokémon. This is accomplished through the VisuStella's "Party System". The Trainer can never be switched out. If a new Pokémon is selected, the Pokémon's turn is skipped.
How can I set it so that you must have a full party to continue, without it mattering which party member it actually is?
How can I make it so the Pokémon's turn is skipped?
"Item", which allows them to, well, use an item. If an item is used, the Pokémon's turn is skipped.
How can I make it so the Pokémon's turn is skipped?
"Encourage", which allows them to shout something to the Pokémon that may or may not have effect on them. Most of the time, it does nothing (and there might be an encouragement that does nothing all the time), but depending several conditions – the Pokémon's current mood, the type it is, what type it's opponent it, etc. – it can (not "will") cause either a positive or negative effect on them. These effects include (but are not limited to): Power Up, Power Down, Having a Random Move Regain One Use, Having a Random Move Decrease One Use, etc. How often this happens (maybe) depends on how close the Trainer is with the Pokémon. (It could also be random, I haven't decided yet.)
"Flee", which which is the "Run Away" option (it doesn't always work).
Once the Trainer has done one of these things (in the case of "Flee", only if the attempt failed), the turn moves to the Pokémon.
The Pokémon has 4 moves, unique to each Pokémon. These moves don't change. There are no TMs or HMs in the game, and the Pokémon don't learn new moves as they level up.
This is mostly because I don't want to bother with new moves, but also because it wouldn't make much sense for the story of the game. (Though I can change my mind on this. It isn't really relevant to what I'm asking here, though.)
The 4 moves have a limit to how many uses they have, and once those are used up, the move can't be used anymore. For this, I am using VisuStella's "Limited Skill Uses". Moves are refilled every time you heal your Pokémon at a Pokémon Center, or sometimes through the "Encourage" command. You also have Items that refresh moves.
At the bottom of the list for every Pokémon is "Struggle", which has no cost, and can be done at any time. However, this move costs health to use, and you can KO yourself with it, so it is not advised.
After you have selected your attack, it depends on your speed which of the two goes first, you or your opponent. If your opponent KOs you, your turn is lost. When the turn comes back to the Trainer, the game automatically makes you pick a new Pokémon. This DOES use up the Trainers turn, but not the Pokémon's.
How can I set it so that you must have a full party to continue, without it mattering which party member it actually is?
How do I check whether the Pokémon has been KOed (died)? You can only check if a specific character has died, rather than any character in a specific slot. Is there any way to check this?
If all Pokémon fall, the battle ends. You go back to the last checkpoint (usually the last Pokémon Centre you stayed at), and your Pokémon are healed automatically. In the case of Trainer Battles, you also lose a bit of money.
How do I check if all Pokémon in the party are KOed (dead)?
I own pretty much all of the VisuStella Plugins already, so it's no problem pointing me to one of them. Otherwise, what Plugin should I use? Are there any problems I didn't think of? I have pretty much no experience with coding using actual code, only the commands, so any code I would have to use would have to be written for me. Currently, I am planning on using the standard battle system, though I could be pursuaded to use a different one. If there is anything you don't get, feel free to ask.

Alternatively, perhaps search for a CTB battles system similar to Final Fantasy X. You can utilize the swap in mechanic from that.

posts.author: Rvanbergen
posts.body:
I have come up with a potential system in case a Pokémon falls in battle. I would very much like it if anyone could check if I made any errors:
Create a Variable for keeping track of who is in the party.
Update that Variable in Common Event "Pok Party". Example: If Pkmn 1 is in the party, it's 1, if Pkmn 2, it's 2, etc.
Create a Variable that keeps track of how big your party is supposed to be. One Pokémon = 1, two Pokémon = 2, etc. Update this variable as you proceed through the game. (The game is not a standard Pokémon game, so I don't need to keep track of every Pokémon. Only 4 to 6)
Create a Common Event called "Battle Loss", and dictate what you want to happen if you lose all Pokémon.
Create a Common Event with several conditional branches for each of the sizes of your party.
If you have only one Pokémon, if it falls, call the "Battle Loss" Event.
If you have 2 Pokémon, what happens next is determined by which Pokémon is in the party.
First, you set a Label by the name of "Party Size 2".
If Pokémon 1 is in the party, check if it is dead.
If not, End Event Processing.
If it is dead, check if Pokémon 2 is dead.
If it is, you have ran out of usable Pokémon. Call the "Battle Loss" Event.
If it is not, call the "Party Scene". Afterwards, call Common Event "Pok Party". Then jump back to the Label named "Party Size 2".
If Pokémon 2 is in the party, check if it is dead.
If not, End Event Processing.
If it is dead, check if Pokémon 1 is dead.
If it is, you have ran out of usable Pokémon. Call the "Battle Loss" Event.
If it is not, call the "Party Scene". Afterwards, call Common Event "Pok Party". Then jump back to the Label named "Party Size 2".
Etc.
By doing things this way, if the Player doesn't switch out their Pokémon, the system detects it and calls up the "Party Scene" again. If the Player
has
switched their Pokémon, the system will end the process, and the battle will continue as normal.
Call the Common Event at the start of every turn.
